text: The page in one screen LangChain is a Python (and TypeScript) library of building blocks for model applications: one interface for every provider's chat model, tools, and since version 1.0 a ready agent loop, create_agent , customised with middleware (code that runs before or after each model or tool call).
label: core
key: one interface for models, tools and retrievers

text: LangGraph is the runtime underneath: you describe a program as a graph of steps (nodes) that read and update one shared state , and LangGraph runs it in rounds called super-steps , saving a checkpoint of the state after each one.
label: core
key: rounds of parallel steps over one shared state

text: The 1.0 announcement put the split in one line each: LangChain is "the fastest way to build an AI agent", LangGraph "a lower level framework and runtime, useful for highly custom and controllable agents" ( LangChain, 22 Oct 2025 ).
label: volatile
key: the fastest way to build an AI agent

text: The reason to use LangGraph rather than the thirty-line loop of the Topic: agentic-frameworks Reading tab is almost entirely the checkpoint: it is what lets a run survive a crash, wait days for a person, and be rewound.
label: core
key: surviving a crash, waiting days for a person and rewinding are all that checkpoint

text: So this page spends most of its time on what a checkpoint holds and what it does and does not save you from, measured.

text: A graph from zero Start from the problem.
label: fat

text: The running example's tests fail because of two bugs.
label: core

text: A sensible workflow: run the tests, diagnose each failure (the two diagnoses are independent, so they can run at the same time), propose one fix from both diagnoses, show the fix to a person, and apply it only if they approve.
label: core

text: In plain Python that is five function calls in a row.
label: fat

text: LangGraph asks you to write the same thing as three kinds of object: State : a typed dictionary (a TypedDict , Pydantic model or dataclass) that every step reads and updates.
label: core

text: Here: the code, the test output, a list of diagnoses, the patch, the decision.
label: core
key: the diagnoses, the patch, the decision

text: Nodes : plain functions that take the state and return a partial update , a dictionary with only the keys they change.
label: core

text: A node never mutates the state it was given.
label: core
key: A node never mutates the state

text: Edges : which node runs after which.
label: core

text: A normal edge always fires; a conditional edge calls a function on the state and returns the name of the next node (or several, or END ).
label: core

text: This is the graph that the Crash lab ran with real Claude Haiku 4.5 calls, trimmed to its shape (the full script is in this page's src/code/e6_real.py ): class S(TypedDict, total=False): core: str test_output: str diagnoses: Annotated[list, operator.add] # a reducer: parallel writes are concatenated patch: str decision: str passed: bool b = StateGraph(S) b.add_node("read_and_test", read_and_test) # returns {"core": ..., "test_output": ...} b.add_node("diagnose_word_count", diag("test_word_count")) b.add_node("diagnose_top_words", diag("test_top_words")) b.add_node("propose_fix", propose_fix) # one model call, returns {"patch": ...} b.add_node("human_review", human_review) # calls interrupt(), returns {"decision": ...} b.add_node("apply_and_test", apply_and_test) b.add_edge(START, "read_and_test") b.add_edge("read_and_test", "diagnose_word_count") # two edges out of one node: b.add_edge("read_and_test", "diagnose_top_words") # both run, in parallel b.add_edge(["diagnose_word_count", "diagnose_top_words"], "propose_fix") # wait for both b.add_edge("propose_fix", "human_review") b.add_edge("human_review", "apply_and_test") b.add_edge("apply_and_test", END) app = b.compile(checkpointer=SqliteSaver(conn)) # the checkpointer is what makes it durable app.invoke({}, {"configurable": {"thread_id": "fix-1"}}) compile() checks the wiring (an edge to an unknown node raises ValueError: Found edge ending at unknown node ; a node that no edge reaches compiles without complaint MEASURED ) and returns a Pregel object, the runtime of section 3.
label: core

text: It has invoke (run to the end or to the next interrupt), stream (the same, yielding events as it goes), get_state and get_state_history (read checkpoints) and update_state (write one, which is how you edit or rewind).
label: core

text: Every call carries a config whose thread_id names the run; with a checkpointer it is required ("you must specify a thread_id ", docs ).
label: core

text: Dashed arrows are conditional edges; solid ones always fire.
label: core

text: START and END are not nodes you write: START is where the input enters, and reaching END with nothing else scheduled ends the run.
label: core
key: reaching END with nothing else scheduled

text: A second way to write the same thing is the functional API (stable since langgraph 0.2.74, 19 Feb 2025, release notes ): ordinary Python control flow inside a function marked @entrypoint , calling functions marked @task whose results are saved.
label: volatile

text: Section 9 shows a measured example.
label: fat

text: Both compile to the same runtime: "Compiling a StateGraph or creating an @entrypoint produces a Pregel instance" ( docs ).
label: core

text: How a graph runs: super-steps LangGraph's README says it "is inspired by Pregel and Apache Beam".
label: core
key: inspired by Pregel and Apache Beam

text: Pregel is Google's system for computing over huge graphs ( Malewicz et al., SIGMOD 2010 ); it runs in the bulk synchronous parallel style that Valiant described in 1990 ( CACM 33(8) ): work proceeds in rounds, everything in a round runs in parallel, and results are exchanged only at the barrier between rounds.
label: core

text: LangGraph calls a round a super-step : "a single tick of the graph where all nodes scheduled for that step execute (potentially in parallel)" ( docs ).
label: core
key: a single tick of the graph

text: Each super-step has three phases, which you can read straight out of pregel/_algo.py : Plan.
label: core

text: Every state key is a channel with a version number that goes up each time it is written.
label: core
key: version number that rises on each write

text: Edges are channels too, with names you never typed: branch:to:propose_fix , or join:diagnose_word_count+diagnose_top_words:propose_fix for a wait-for-both edge.
label: core

text: Each node remembers the version of each trigger channel it last saw ( versions_seen ).
label: core

text: A node runs in this step if one of its trigger channels has a newer version than it saw.
label: core
key: runs in this step if one has a newer version

text: All triggered nodes run in parallel.
label: core
key: All triggered nodes run in parallel

text: Each reads the state as it was at the start of the step , so no node sees another's output from the same step.
label: core
key: as of the start of the step

text: What a node returns is not applied yet: it is held, and saved, as a pending write .
label: core

text: At the barrier, all pending writes are applied together, sorted by task path rather than by finishing time, each through its channel's reducer; written channels get the next version; and a checkpoint is saved.
label: core
key: sorted by task path rather than finishing time

text: Then the next plan starts.
label: fat

text: When no node is triggered, the run ends.
label: core
key: When no node is triggered, the run ends

text: A key with no reducer is a LastValue channel: it accepts exactly one write per step.
label: core

text: A key annotated with a reducer ( Annotated[list, operator.add] , or add_messages for chat messages) is a BinaryOperatorAggregate channel: any number of writes are folded in.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets A checkpointer is the object you pass to compile(checkpointer=...) ; it saves a checkpoint at every super-step boundary and the pending writes of every task in between.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Without one, the state lives only in the running process, and interrupts cannot be resumed (section 6).
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: With one, a thread's whole history is in a database, keyed by thread_id .
label: core
key: a thread's whole history is in a database

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: What one checkpoint holds (the Checkpoint type in langgraph-checkpoint 4.2.0): id (unique and increasing, so it sorts by time), ts , channel_values (the state, plus trigger channels), channel_versions , versions_seen (per node) and updated_channels .
label: core
key: unique and increasing, so it sorts by time

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Beside it sits metadata: source ( input , loop , update or fork ), step (-1 for the input checkpoint, then 0, 1, 2 ...), the parent checkpoint and the run id.
label: core

text: Postgres (3.1.2, Postgres 16 in Docker): four tables, created by setup() through 10 migrations. checkpoints (small JSONB rows), checkpoint_blobs (one row per channel per version, so an unchanged channel is not stored again), checkpoint_writes and checkpoint_migrations .

text: An EncryptedSerializer encrypts everything with an AES key from LANGGRAPH_AES_KEY ( docs ): checkpoints hold every prompt, tool result and secret your agent saw.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Storage grows with the square of the run length An agent's state is mostly its message list, and the message list changes every step.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: A checkpoint stores the whole list each time, so a run of N steps that adds about the same amount per step stores about N(N+1)/2 copies' worth.

text: LangGraph 1.2 added a beta channel type, DeltaChannel , that stores only each step's new writes and rebuilds the value by replaying them: SQLite Postgres Stored bytes = checkpoint rows + blobs + writes, uncompressed ( length() in SQLite, octet_length() in Postgres).
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Tool results are hex text, different every step, so compression would not hide the growth. get_state times are one call on the M1 Pro; Postgres times include the round trip into Docker.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: So for long agent threads, either keep the message list short (summarise or trim with middleware, section 9, or a context policy ), prune old checkpoints, or try DeltaChannel , whose docstring marks it beta: "The API and on-disk representation may change".
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Its price is on the read side: reading the state replays writes.
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: Durability modes: when the checkpoint is written invoke(..., durability=...) takes one of three values ( docs ): "sync" persists "synchronously before the next step starts"; "async" , the default in the source, persists "asynchronously while the next step executes", with a "small risk" of losing a checkpoint in a crash; "exit" persists "only when graph execution exits", so "you cannot recover from system failures (like process crashes) mid-execution".
label: core

section: 4. checkpointers: what is saved, where, and how big it gets
text: The cost of each, on a one-node loop of 200 super-steps (best of 3) MEASURED : A fraction of a millisecond per step against model calls of seconds: for agents the overhead does not matter, and sync is the safe choice. exit exists for short graphs where you only care about the final state.
label: core

text: What survives a crash Three things can stop a run halfway: the process dies (a deploy, an out-of-memory kill, a laptop lid), a node raises (a provider timeout), or a person has not answered yet.
